    <div dir='auto' class='story__content  flow-root    pt-1 mt-1 text-4 sm:text-4.5  overflow-visible'><p>LAHORE: Intercity bus services from Lahore to several destinations across the country were suspended on Sunday after the administration reportedly sealed all general bus terminals in the city late on Saturday night, leaving passengers stranded and disrupting travel.</p>
<p>The closures affected passengers travelling to Islamabad, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Sindh, southern Punjab and other parts of central Punjab. Several passengers reported difficulties after their tickets were cancelled and transport services suspended.</p>
<p>Meanwhile, major private bus operators, including Faisal Movers and Daewoo, suspended their services amid reports of restrictions on public transport movement on motorways and national highways.</p>
<p>Representatives of Faisal Movers and Daewoo told <em>Dawn</em> that their services had been suspended and buses were not being dispatched due to the restrictions.</p>
<p>However, motorway police spokesperson Imran Shah told <em>Dawn</em> that motorways and highways were open to traffic and that he was unaware of any directions to suspend bus services.</p>
<p>Another motorway police official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said buses were not operating on motorways or highways because of the PTI’s protest call. He added that people travelling in private vehicles could use the roads.</p>
<p>Punjab Transport Department Secretary Imran Sikandar Baloch was unavailable for comment despite repeated attempts to contact him on his mobile phone.</p>
<p>The development comes as the PTI launched its march on October 4 despite warnings from the Centre.</p>
<p>So far, the march — being carried out to demand Imran’s release — has remained within KP, where the PTI is in power.</p>
<p>A day earlier, containers were transported to Swabi Interchange — where the PTI had <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2036185">called</a> on its workers to gather — as well as the Indus River bridge on the M-1 Motorway to block the party’s march, but the motorway and the Grand Trunk Road remain open to traffic.</p>

headline: Intercity transport suspended in Lahore, bus terminals reportedly sealed
description: Major private bus operators, including Faisal Movers and Daewoo, suspend services amid reported restrictions on public transport.
author: Imran Gabol
article_text:
LAHORE: Intercity bus services from Lahore to several destinations across the country were suspended on Sunday after the administration reportedly sealed all general bus terminals in the city late on Saturday night, leaving passengers stranded and disrupting travel.

The closures affected passengers travelling to Islamabad, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Sindh, southern Punjab and other parts of central Punjab. Several passengers reported difficulties after their tickets were cancelled and transport services suspended.

Meanwhile, major private bus operators, including Faisal Movers and Daewoo, suspended their services amid reports of restrictions on public transport movement on motorways and national highways.

Representatives of Faisal Movers and Daewoo told Dawn that their services had been suspended and buses were not being dispatched due to the restrictions.

However, motorway police spokesperson Imran Shah told Dawn that motorways and highways were open to traffic and that he was unaware of any directions to suspend bus services.

Another motorway police official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said buses were not operating on motorways or highways because of the PTI’s protest call. He added that people travelling in private vehicles could use the roads.

Punjab Transport Department Secretary Imran Sikandar Baloch was unavailable for comment despite repeated attempts to contact him on his mobile phone.

The development comes as the PTI launched its march on October 4 despite warnings from the Centre.

So far, the march — being carried out to demand Imran’s release — has remained within KP, where the PTI is in power.

A day earlier, containers were transported to Swabi Interchange — where the PTI had called on its workers to gather — as well as the Indus River bridge on the M-1 Motorway to block the party’s march, but the motorway and the Grand Trunk Road remain open to traffic.

        function handleEagerSlots() {
            var prebidEnabled = false;

                var slotId = eagerSlot.id;
                if (slotId) {
                    

                    // When Prebid is disabled, GPT's native lazy-loader will automatically

                    if (!prebidEnabled) {
                        if (window.__debugAds) { console.log('EagerLoad: skipping refresh() — GPT lazy-loader handles ATF: ' + slotId); }

                    // Find the slot by element ID directly

                    if (slot) {

                        googletag.pubads().refresh([slot]);

            const INVIEW_THRESHOLD = 30;
            const WAIT_TIMEOUT = 3000;
            const delayedIds = new Set();

            const log = (label, extra = '') =>
                window.__debugAds && console.log(new Date().toISOString().substr(11, 8) + ' ' + label + '(' + extra + ')');

            const getMatchingSlots = id =>
                googletag.pubads().getSlots().filter(
                    slot => slot.getAdUnitPath() === id || slot.getSlotElementId() === id
                );
            
            // no smart refresh, just refresh the ad after x seconds

                log('dumb refreshAd', id + '!!');
                googletag.pubads().refresh(getMatchingSlots(id));
                return;
            }

            function attemptRefresh(id, doRefresh, remainingTimeout = 3000) {
                log('delayedRefresh', id + ', ' + doRefresh + ', ' + remainingTimeout);

                if (doRefresh && !delayedIds.has(id)) {
                    if (remainingTimeout === 0) {
                        log('refreshAd', id + '!!');
                        googletag.pubads().refresh(getMatchingSlots(id));
                        return;
                    }
                    
                    delayedIds.add(id);
                    
                    setTimeout(() => {
                        if (!delayedIds.has(id)) return;

                        delayedIds.delete(id);
                        const percent = percentageInView(id);
                        attemptRefresh(id, percent >= INVIEW_THRESHOLD, remainingTimeout - 1000);
                    }, WAIT_TIMEOUT);

                if (!doRefresh) {
                    delayedIds.delete(id);
                    setTimeout(() => refreshAd(id, true), 1000);

            log('refreshAd', id);

            const slots = getMatchingSlots(id);
            for (const slot of slots) {
                const percent = percentageInView(id);

                // smart refresh recurrsive function to handle ad refreshing

                attemptRefresh(id, percent >= INVIEW_THRESHOLD);

        window.percentageInView = ((id) => {
            const element = document.getElementById(id);
            if (!element) {
                return 0;

            let adRect = element.getBoundingClientRect();
            
            let needsHiding = false;
            if (adRect.x == 0) {
                adRect = element.getBoundingClientRect();
                element.style.display = 'block';
                needsHiding = true;
                
            }
            
            // Calculate visible vertical height
            const visibleHeight = Math.min(adRect.bottom, window.innerHeight) - Math.max(adRect.top, 0);

            // Ensure visibility is non-negative
            const clampedVisibleHeight = Math.max(0, visibleHeight);
            const totalHeight = adRect.height;

            // Calculate vertical percentage in view
            const percentageInView = totalHeight > 0 ? (clampedVisibleHeight / totalHeight) * 100 : 0;

            if (needsHiding) element.style.display = 'none';
            
            return percentageInView;

    <div dir='auto' class='story__content  flow-root    pt-1 mt-1 text-4 sm:text-4.5  overflow-visible'><p>ISLAMABAD: The federal government on Sunday authorised the deployment of Pakistan Army troops and assets in aid of civil power in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, after <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2036352/emergency-governors-rule-imposed-in-kp-as-president-approves-cabinet-decision">imposing </a>an emergency and governor’s rule in the province.</p>
<p>The authorisation of the army deployment was made through Statutory Regulatory Order, issued by the interior ministry on Sunday.</p>
<p>According to the order, a copy of which is available with <em>Dawn</em>, the federal government authorised the deployment of army troops and assets in aid of civil power for the “safety of life, security of persons and property of citizens as well as security of government installations” in the province.</p>
<p>The authorisation lasts for the duration of the proclamation issued regarding the imposition of an emergency and governor’s rule. The notification cited powers conferred to the government under Article 245 of the Constitution.</p>
<p>KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi, in consultation with the Military Operations Directorate at General Headquarters in Rawalpindi, would determine the number of troops and assets necessary, the notification added.</p>
<p>Copies of the order were forwarded to the president’s secretary, prime minister’s adviser, the KP governor’s secretary, the Military Operations Directorate GHQ Rawalpindi, the KP home secretary, the inspector general of police (IGP) in the province, the Peshawar High Court registrar and other officials.</p>
<p>The emergency imposition comes a day after <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2036160">PM Shehbaz met President Zardari</a> and discussed the country’s overall security situation.</p>
<p>That meeting came amid heightened tensions between the PML-N-led federal government and the KP government led by the PTI — which is in opposition in the Centre. They have been at odds over various issues, particularly on the counterterrorism policy, which was one of the main <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2034734/pti-terms-access-to-imran-principal-point-of-deadlock-claims-centre-refused-to-include-it-in-agreement"><u>reasons</u></a> behind the <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2034693/naqvi-says-talks-with-opposition-have-collapsed-accuses-kp-cm-of-sabotaging-negotiations"><u>breakdown</u></a> of their <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2034465/after-hours-of-negotiations-second-round-of-govt-opposition-talks-ends-in-a-deadlock"><u>Oct 3 talks</u></a>.</p>
    <figure class='media  w-full  sm:w-full  media--  ' data-original-src='https://i.dawn.com/primary/2026/10/11194814a275cda.webp'>
        <div class='media__item  '><picture><img src='https://i.dawn.com/primary/2026/10/11194814a275cda.webp'  alt='Police guard a road leading to Red Zone, in Peshawar on October 11, 2026. — Reuters' /></picture></div>
        <figcaption class='media__caption  '>Police guard a road leading to Red Zone, in Peshawar on October 11, 2026. — Reuters</figcaption>
    </figure>
<p>The PTI has said it was being left out of security decisions concerning KP, which the Centre has <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2035383#:~:text=being%20left%20out%20of%20decisions%20concerning%20the%20Centre%E2%80%99s%20counterterrorism%20policy%20was%20%E2%80%9Ccompletely%20wrong%E2%80%9D%20and%20%E2%80%9Cmisleading"><u>denied</u></a>. It also calls for reviewing the counterterrorism policy and opposes military operations.</p>
<p>On the other hand, the Centre has been <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2033266"><u>criticising</u></a> the KP government’s efforts to combat terrorism in the province and objects to its <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2032947"><u>stance</u></a> on dialogue with the Afghan Taliban.</p>
<h2><a id="shipping-containers-block-roads" href="#shipping-containers-block-roads" class="heading-permalink" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1" title="Permalink"></a>Shipping containers block roads</h2>
<p>Shipping containers were placed around the city of Peshawar to block roads after the imposition of the emergency.</p>
<p>Containers were placed near Peshawar’s railway station to block the routes towards Khyber Bazaar, Shoba Bazaar and beyond. They were also placed near Edwardes College to block entry to Jail Road and Malik Saad Shaheed Flyover, while people were turned away from Sher Shah Suri Road as it was reported to be completely closed.</p>
<p>Police were reportedly deployed in significant numbers, particularly around Governor House. The deployment included personnel called from other districts.</p>
<p>Police and personnel of law enforcement agencies (LEAs), including many in plainclothes, were seen patrolling the roads leading to Governor House, the central police office, Peshawar police headquarters and other government installations largely located in the Red Zone, a correspondent reported.</p>
<p>Vehicles with tinted glasses, police mobile vans, armored personnel carriers and other LEA vehicles were reportedly the only transport visible in and around the cantonment area, with life at a standstill and the area appearing deserted.</p>
<p>Another correspondent reported that the road leading to Khyber Road was shuttered by a container and the traffic control gate closed. A large number of police personnel were also seen around Surey Pul, a favoured spot for protesters.</p>
<p>Grand Trunk (GT) Road was blocked by containers at Firdous Chowk and the correspondent reported a large number of police personnel in the area. Only pedestrians were allowed to move ahead.</p>
<p>Additionally, containers near Bala Hisar Fort and outside the Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) office on Arbab Road blocked entry towards Mall Road.</p>
    <figure class='media  w-full  sm:w-full  media--  ' data-original-src='https://i.dawn.com/primary/2026/10/11170544bb8b8bf.webp'>
        <div class='media__item  '><picture><img src='https://i.dawn.com/primary/2026/10/11170544bb8b8bf.webp'  alt='A vehicle moves past a shipping container used to block a road leading to the Red Zone, in Peshawar on October 11, 2026. — Reuters' /></picture></div>
        <figcaption class='media__caption  '>A vehicle moves past a shipping container used to block a road leading to the Red Zone, in Peshawar on October 11, 2026. — Reuters</figcaption>
    </figure>
<p>Only official vehicles were being allowed to travel from Governor House towards the Chief Minister’s House, while tight security was reported on Sahibzada Abdul Qayyum road where they are located. The Civil Secretariat was seen to be deserted.</p>
<p>Royal Artillery (RA) Bazaar has been closed, while Saddar remains partially open.</p>
<p>Additionally, Peshawar’s Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) stations were reported to be shuttered by <em>Dawn</em>’s correspondent.</p>
<p>The stretch of Khyber Road connecting to University Road and Airport Road at Aman Chowk was reported to be open but with low traffic. A large police contingent was seen at Aman Chowk. Meanwhile, University Road was blocked by containers at Tehkal, and containers at Stadium Chowk allowed for only single-file passage of vehicles on both sides.</p>
<p>Earlier, traffic jams were reported due to the closure of Khyber Road, which connects GT Road with the eastern side of University Road and serves as the main artery and choke point. The resulting diversions created pressure on auxiliary roads.</p>
<p>The area is part of the cantonment, and the Red Zone contains important installations such as the Corps Commander’s House, civil secretariat, central police office, CM Secretariat, CM House and Governor House.</p>
<p>All telecoms services, including landline and DSL, are reported to be suspended in the provincial capital. The city had witnessed a nearly 48-hour mobile service blackout just days ago, on account of the presence of the PTI in the city for its <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2035662">long march</a>.</p>
<p>With networks suspended, people faced immense issues in withdrawing money from bank accounts, as ATMs remained out of service for the entire day.</p>
<p>Aside from the suspension of cellular network and broadband services, however, the situation remained normal for those living on Kohat Road, Charsadda Road, GT Road beyond Pir Zakorhi Bridge, and the area bordering the Khyber district, as well as others on the outskirts of the provincial capital. Vehicles of the armed forces were also reported to be patrolling cantonment areas and a heavy deployment of police was reported in both the city and its outskirts including Kohat Road, GT Road, University Road and Warsak Road.</p>
<p>On Saturday, KP Inspector General of Police (IGP) Zulfiqar Hameed put district police on <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2036342/kp-police-put-on-alert-as-emergency-looms">alert</a> for possible violent protests and sabotage in the event of an emergency in the province, emphasising caution in the use of force.</p>
    <figure class='media  w-full  sm:w-full  media--  ' data-original-src='https://i.dawn.com/primary/2026/10/1119453545fc103.webp'>
        <div class='media__item  '><picture><img src='https://i.dawn.com/primary/2026/10/1119453545fc103.webp'  alt='Police personnel stand guard near shipping containers blocking a road leading to the Red Zone in Peshawar on October 11, 2026. — Reuters' /></picture></div>
        <figcaption class='media__caption  '>Police personnel stand guard near shipping containers blocking a road leading to the Red Zone in Peshawar on October 11, 2026. — Reuters</figcaption>
    </figure>
<p>A notification issued by the IGP’s office directed not only officers in Peshawar but also district police officers (DPOs), sub-divisional police officers (SDPOs) and even station house officers (SHOs) to personally monitor the situation.</p>
<p>It said DPOs could issue appropriate directions, instructions or guidelines to regulate protests and ensure public safety. In the event of violence, they could also take necessary legal action.</p>
<p>It added that the use of force was to be carried out on a gradated basis, noting that in the first phase, protesters should be clearly warned against violence before police began to use forceful measures.</p>
<h2><a id="kp-house-sealed-npc-refuses-to-allow-ttap-presser" href="#kp-house-sealed-npc-refuses-to-allow-ttap-presser" class="heading-permalink" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1" title="Permalink"></a>KP House sealed, NPC refuses to allow TTAP presser</h2>
<p>In Islamabad, the main opposition alliance — which would typically hold pressers at KP House — could not find a place to hold a press conference in the urban areas as KP House was sealed.</p>
<p>The Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP) has therefore decided to hold its presser at Jamia Al Wilaya near Bhara Kahu on the Murree Expressway.</p>
<p>Speaking to <em>Dawn</em>, TTAP spokesperson Akhunzada Hussain Ahmed Yousafzai said that after deciding to hold a press conference, the alliance initially thought to go to KP House, but came to know that it had been sealed.</p>
<p>He added that they then decided to hold it at the National Press Club (NPC), but were refused by the club despite being willing to pay the fee.</p>
<p>“Now we have decided to hold the presser at Bhara Kahu,” he said.</p>

headline: Pakistan Army deployed in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in aid of civil power
description: Shipping containers placed in Peshawar; police reportedly deployed in significant numbers, particularly around Governor House.
author: Umer Farooq, Ismail Khan, Ikram Junaidi, Iftikhar A. Khan, Manzoor Ali
article_text:
ISLAMABAD: The federal government on Sunday authorised the deployment of Pakistan Army troops and assets in aid of civil power in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, after imposing an emergency and governor’s rule in the province.

The authorisation of the army deployment was made through Statutory Regulatory Order, issued by the interior ministry on Sunday.

According to the order, a copy of which is available with Dawn, the federal government authorised the deployment of army troops and assets in aid of civil power for the “safety of life, security of persons and property of citizens as well as security of government installations” in the province.

The authorisation lasts for the duration of the proclamation issued regarding the imposition of an emergency and governor’s rule. The notification cited powers conferred to the government under Article 245 of the Constitution.

KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi, in consultation with the Military Operations Directorate at General Headquarters in Rawalpindi, would determine the number of troops and assets necessary, the notification added.

Copies of the order were forwarded to the president’s secretary, prime minister’s adviser, the KP governor’s secretary, the Military Operations Directorate GHQ Rawalpindi, the KP home secretary, the inspector general of police (IGP) in the province, the Peshawar High Court registrar and other officials.

The emergency imposition comes a day after PM Shehbaz met President Zardari and discussed the country’s overall security situation.

That meeting came amid heightened tensions between the PML-N-led federal government and the KP government led by the PTI — which is in opposition in the Centre. They have been at odds over various issues, particularly on the counterterrorism policy, which was one of the main reasons behind the breakdown of their Oct 3 talks.

The PTI has said it was being left out of security decisions concerning KP, which the Centre has denied. It also calls for reviewing the counterterrorism policy and opposes military operations.

On the other hand, the Centre has been criticising the KP government’s efforts to combat terrorism in the province and objects to its stance on dialogue with the Afghan Taliban.

Shipping containers block roads

Shipping containers were placed around the city of Peshawar to block roads after the imposition of the emergency.

Containers were placed near Peshawar’s railway station to block the routes towards Khyber Bazaar, Shoba Bazaar and beyond. They were also placed near Edwardes College to block entry to Jail Road and Malik Saad Shaheed Flyover, while people were turned away from Sher Shah Suri Road as it was reported to be completely closed.

Police were reportedly deployed in significant numbers, particularly around Governor House. The deployment included personnel called from other districts.

Police and personnel of law enforcement agencies (LEAs), including many in plainclothes, were seen patrolling the roads leading to Governor House, the central police office, Peshawar police headquarters and other government installations largely located in the Red Zone, a correspondent reported.

Vehicles with tinted glasses, police mobile vans, armored personnel carriers and other LEA vehicles were reportedly the only transport visible in and around the cantonment area, with life at a standstill and the area appearing deserted.

Another correspondent reported that the road leading to Khyber Road was shuttered by a container and the traffic control gate closed. A large number of police personnel were also seen around Surey Pul, a favoured spot for protesters.

Grand Trunk (GT) Road was blocked by containers at Firdous Chowk and the correspondent reported a large number of police personnel in the area. Only pedestrians were allowed to move ahead.

Additionally, containers near Bala Hisar Fort and outside the Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) office on Arbab Road blocked entry towards Mall Road.

Only official vehicles were being allowed to travel from Governor House towards the Chief Minister’s House, while tight security was reported on Sahibzada Abdul Qayyum road where they are located. The Civil Secretariat was seen to be deserted.

Royal Artillery (RA) Bazaar has been closed, while Saddar remains partially open.

Additionally, Peshawar’s Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) stations were reported to be shuttered by Dawn’s correspondent.

The stretch of Khyber Road connecting to University Road and Airport Road at Aman Chowk was reported to be open but with low traffic. A large police contingent was seen at Aman Chowk. Meanwhile, University Road was blocked by containers at Tehkal, and containers at Stadium Chowk allowed for only single-file passage of vehicles on both sides.

Earlier, traffic jams were reported due to the closure of Khyber Road, which connects GT Road with the eastern side of University Road and serves as the main artery and choke point. The resulting diversions created pressure on auxiliary roads.

The area is part of the cantonment, and the Red Zone contains important installations such as the Corps Commander’s House, civil secretariat, central police office, CM Secretariat, CM House and Governor House.

All telecoms services, including landline and DSL, are reported to be suspended in the provincial capital. The city had witnessed a nearly 48-hour mobile service blackout just days ago, on account of the presence of the PTI in the city for its long march.

With networks suspended, people faced immense issues in withdrawing money from bank accounts, as ATMs remained out of service for the entire day.

Aside from the suspension of cellular network and broadband services, however, the situation remained normal for those living on Kohat Road, Charsadda Road, GT Road beyond Pir Zakorhi Bridge, and the area bordering the Khyber district, as well as others on the outskirts of the provincial capital. Vehicles of the armed forces were also reported to be patrolling cantonment areas and a heavy deployment of police was reported in both the city and its outskirts including Kohat Road, GT Road, University Road and Warsak Road.

On Saturday, KP Inspector General of Police (IGP) Zulfiqar Hameed put district police on alert for possible violent protests and sabotage in the event of an emergency in the province, emphasising caution in the use of force.

A notification issued by the IGP’s office directed not only officers in Peshawar but also district police officers (DPOs), sub-divisional police officers (SDPOs) and even station house officers (SHOs) to personally monitor the situation.

It said DPOs could issue appropriate directions, instructions or guidelines to regulate protests and ensure public safety. In the event of violence, they could also take necessary legal action.

It added that the use of force was to be carried out on a gradated basis, noting that in the first phase, protesters should be clearly warned against violence before police began to use forceful measures.

KP House sealed, NPC refuses to allow TTAP presser

In Islamabad, the main opposition alliance — which would typically hold pressers at KP House — could not find a place to hold a press conference in the urban areas as KP House was sealed.

The Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP) has therefore decided to hold its presser at Jamia Al Wilaya near Bhara Kahu on the Murree Expressway.

Speaking to Dawn, TTAP spokesperson Akhunzada Hussain Ahmed Yousafzai said that after deciding to hold a press conference, the alliance initially thought to go to KP House, but came to know that it had been sealed.

He added that they then decided to hold it at the National Press Club (NPC), but were refused by the club despite being willing to pay the fee.

“Now we have decided to hold the presser at Bhara Kahu,” he said.

article_html:
ISLAMABAD: The federal government on Sunday authorised the deployment of Pakistan Army troops and assets in aid of civil power in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, after imposing an emergency and governor’s rule in the province.

The authorisation of the army deployment was made through Statutory Regulatory Order, issued by the interior ministry on Sunday.

According to the order, a copy of which is available with Dawn, the federal government authorised the deployment of army troops and assets in aid of civil power for the “safety of life, security of persons and property of citizens as well as security of government installations” in the province.

The authorisation lasts for the duration of the proclamation issued regarding the imposition of an emergency and governor’s rule. The notification cited powers conferred to the government under Article 245 of the Constitution.

KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi, in consultation with the Military Operations Directorate at General Headquarters in Rawalpindi, would determine the number of troops and assets necessary, the notification added.

Copies of the order were forwarded to the president’s secretary, prime minister’s adviser, the KP governor’s secretary, the Military Operations Directorate GHQ Rawalpindi, the KP home secretary, the inspector general of police (IGP) in the province, the Peshawar High Court registrar and other officials.

The emergency imposition comes a day after PM Shehbaz met President Zardari and discussed the country’s overall security situation.

That meeting came amid heightened tensions between the PML-N-led federal government and the KP government led by the PTI — which is in opposition in the Centre. They have been at odds over various issues, particularly on the counterterrorism policy, which was one of the main reasons behind the breakdown of their Oct 3 talks.

The PTI has said it was being left out of security decisions concerning KP, which the Centre has denied. It also calls for reviewing the counterterrorism policy and opposes military operations.

On the other hand, the Centre has been criticising the KP government’s efforts to combat terrorism in the province and objects to its stance on dialogue with the Afghan Taliban.

Shipping containers block roads

Shipping containers were placed around the city of Peshawar to block roads after the imposition of the emergency.

Containers were placed near Peshawar’s railway station to block the routes towards Khyber Bazaar, Shoba Bazaar and beyond. They were also placed near Edwardes College to block entry to Jail Road and Malik Saad Shaheed Flyover, while people were turned away from Sher Shah Suri Road as it was reported to be completely closed.

Police were reportedly deployed in significant numbers, particularly around Governor House. The deployment included personnel called from other districts.

Police and personnel of law enforcement agencies (LEAs), including many in plainclothes, were seen patrolling the roads leading to Governor House, the central police office, Peshawar police headquarters and other government installations largely located in the Red Zone, a correspondent reported.

Vehicles with tinted glasses, police mobile vans, armored personnel carriers and other LEA vehicles were reportedly the only transport visible in and around the cantonment area, with life at a standstill and the area appearing deserted.

Another correspondent reported that the road leading to Khyber Road was shuttered by a container and the traffic control gate closed. A large number of police personnel were also seen around Surey Pul, a favoured spot for protesters.

Grand Trunk (GT) Road was blocked by containers at Firdous Chowk and the correspondent reported a large number of police personnel in the area. Only pedestrians were allowed to move ahead.

Additionally, containers near Bala Hisar Fort and outside the Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) office on Arbab Road blocked entry towards Mall Road.

Only official vehicles were being allowed to travel from Governor House towards the Chief Minister’s House, while tight security was reported on Sahibzada Abdul Qayyum road where they are located. The Civil Secretariat was seen to be deserted.

Royal Artillery (RA) Bazaar has been closed, while Saddar remains partially open.

Additionally, Peshawar’s Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) stations were reported to be shuttered by Dawn’s correspondent.

The stretch of Khyber Road connecting to University Road and Airport Road at Aman Chowk was reported to be open but with low traffic. A large police contingent was seen at Aman Chowk. Meanwhile, University Road was blocked by containers at Tehkal, and containers at Stadium Chowk allowed for only single-file passage of vehicles on both sides.

Earlier, traffic jams were reported due to the closure of Khyber Road, which connects GT Road with the eastern side of University Road and serves as the main artery and choke point. The resulting diversions created pressure on auxiliary roads.

The area is part of the cantonment, and the Red Zone contains important installations such as the Corps Commander’s House, civil secretariat, central police office, CM Secretariat, CM House and Governor House.

All telecoms services, including landline and DSL, are reported to be suspended in the provincial capital. The city had witnessed a nearly 48-hour mobile service blackout just days ago, on account of the presence of the PTI in the city for its long march.

With networks suspended, people faced immense issues in withdrawing money from bank accounts, as ATMs remained out of service for the entire day.

Aside from the suspension of cellular network and broadband services, however, the situation remained normal for those living on Kohat Road, Charsadda Road, GT Road beyond Pir Zakorhi Bridge, and the area bordering the Khyber district, as well as others on the outskirts of the provincial capital. Vehicles of the armed forces were also reported to be patrolling cantonment areas and a heavy deployment of police was reported in both the city and its outskirts including Kohat Road, GT Road, University Road and Warsak Road.

On Saturday, KP Inspector General of Police (IGP) Zulfiqar Hameed put district police on alert for possible violent protests and sabotage in the event of an emergency in the province, emphasising caution in the use of force.

A notification issued by the IGP’s office directed not only officers in Peshawar but also district police officers (DPOs), sub-divisional police officers (SDPOs) and even station house officers (SHOs) to personally monitor the situation.

It said DPOs could issue appropriate directions, instructions or guidelines to regulate protests and ensure public safety. In the event of violence, they could also take necessary legal action.

It added that the use of force was to be carried out on a gradated basis, noting that in the first phase, protesters should be clearly warned against violence before police began to use forceful measures.

KP House sealed, NPC refuses to allow TTAP presser

In Islamabad, the main opposition alliance — which would typically hold pressers at KP House — could not find a place to hold a press conference in the urban areas as KP House was sealed.

The Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP) has therefore decided to hold its presser at Jamia Al Wilaya near Bhara Kahu on the Murree Expressway.

Speaking to Dawn, TTAP spokesperson Akhunzada Hussain Ahmed Yousafzai said that after deciding to hold a press conference, the alliance initially thought to go to KP House, but came to know that it had been sealed.

He added that they then decided to hold it at the National Press Club (NPC), but were refused by the club despite being willing to pay the fee.

“Now we have decided to hold the presser at Bhara Kahu,” he said.

    <div dir='auto' class='story__content  flow-root    pt-1 mt-1 text-4 sm:text-4.5  overflow-visible'><p>A soldier was martyred and 12 terrorists killed in an exchange of fire in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Kurram district, the army’s media wing said on Sunday.</p>
<p>The Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said that the movement of a group of <em>khawarij</em> attempting to cross the international border from Afghanistan into Pakistan was detected in Kurram district on Sunday, where security forces engaged them effectively.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/1849349/govt-proscribes-gul-bahadur-group-majeed-brigade#:~:text=TTP%20labelled%20as%20fitna"><em><u>Fitna al Khawarij</u></em></a> is a term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan.</p>
    <figure class='media  w-full  w-full  media--  media--embed  media--uneven media--tweet' data-original-src='https://x.com/RadioPakistan/status/2109179952784654680'>
        <div class='media__item  media__item--twitter  '><span>
    <blockquote class="twitter-tweet" lang="en">
        <a href="https://twitter.com/RadioPakistan/status/2109179952784654680"></a>
    </blockquote>
</span></div>
        
    </figure>
<p>Security forces, “maintaining a high state of alertness and vigilance, effectively thwarted the infiltration attempt”, the statement added.</p>
<p>It further said that Afghan Taliban posts had also opened fire to support the infiltration attempt by the khawarij.</p>
<p>“The skilful and precise engagement by vigilant troops resulted in the killing of 12 khawarij and Afghan Taliban,” the statement said. During the exchange of fire, Naib Subedar Hidayat Aman was martyred after “fighting gallantly”.</p>
<p>This incident along the Pakistan-Afghanistan border vindicates Islamabad’s “objective and factual stance regarding the willful abject failure of the Afghan Taliban regime to deny the use of Afghan soil to the terrorist organisation”, the statement added.</p>
<p>“The security forces of Pakistan remain resolute and unwavering in their commitment to defend the nation’s frontiers,” said the ISPR, adding that sanitisation operation is being conducted in the area to eliminate any other Indian sponsored <em>khawariji</em> found in the area.”</p>
<p>“The relentless counter-terrorism campaign under vision Azm-i-Istehkam as approved by Federal Apex Committee on National Action Plan by security forces and law enforcement agencies of Pakistan will continue at full pace to wipe out the menace of foreign sponsored and supported terrorism from the country.”</p>
    <figure class='media  w-full sm:w-1/2  media--right  media--embed  media--uneven' data-original-src='https://www.dawn.com/news/1848738'>
        <div class='media__item  media__item--newskitlink  '>    <iframe
        class="nk-iframe"
        width="100%" frameborder="0" scrolling="no" style="height:250px;position:relative"
        src="https://www.dawn.com/news/card/1848738"
        sandbox="allow-same-origin allow-scripts allow-popups allow-modals allow-forms"></iframe></div>
        
    </figure>
<p>“These sacrifices of our brave soldiers further reinforce our unwavering commitment to safeguarding our nation and its frontiers at all costs,” it said.</p>
<p>In a statement on X, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi paid tribute to the security forces for “foiling the infiltration attempt”.</p>
    <figure class='media  w-full  w-full  media--  media--embed  media--uneven media--tweet' data-original-src='https://x.com/MOIofficialGoP/status/2109177918194651185'>
        <div class='media__item  media__item--twitter  '><span>
    <blockquote class="twitter-tweet" lang="en">
        <a href="https://twitter.com/MOIofficialGoP/status/2109177918194651185"></a>
    </blockquote>
</span></div>
        
    </figure>
<p>He expressed “heartfelt condolences and expression of sympathy” to the bereaved family of the martyred Naib Subedar Hidayat Aman, adding that nation takes pride in the “professional capabilities and courage” of the security forces.</p>
<p>KP has been witnessing terrorist attacks and security challenges for a long time</p>
<p>September particularly witnessed a significant deterioration in Pakistan’s overall security environment, accompanied by growing political, economic and regional pressures, according to <a rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank" class="link--external" href="https://picss.net/reports/picss-monthly-insight-september-2026/"><u>Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS)</u></a>.</p>
<p>Terrorist violence <a rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank" class="link--external" href="https://picss.net/reports/picss-monthly-insight-september-2026/"><u>increased substantially</u></a>, with 225 attacks recorded nationwide, compared with 199 in August, representing a 13.1 per cent increase and the highest monthly total recorded in 12 years.</p>
<p>On <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2032950"><u>Sept 27</u></a>, 14 people, including two rescue officials, were martyred and 35 sustained injuries after a suicide bomber rammed an explosive-laden vehicle into a police checkpost in and then targeted an ambulance taking bodies to hospital in DI Khan.</p>
<p>On Sept 18, a <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2031031"><u>major attack</u></a> in the old Police Lines in KP’s Kohat claimed 23 lives and injured about 100 others. Eight terrorists were killed during an <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2031100"><u>overnight clearance operation</u></a>.</p>

    </div>

headline: Soldier martyred, 12 terrorists killed as security forces foil infiltration attempt in Kurram: ISPR
description: Afghan Taliban posts opened fire to support the infiltration attempt, army's media wing says.
author: News Desk
article_text:
A soldier was martyred and 12 terrorists killed in an exchange of fire in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Kurram district, the army’s media wing said on Sunday.

The Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said that the movement of a group of khawarij attempting to cross the international border from Afghanistan into Pakistan was detected in Kurram district on Sunday, where security forces engaged them effectively.

Fitna al Khawarij is a term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan.

Security forces, “maintaining a high state of alertness and vigilance, effectively thwarted the infiltration attempt”, the statement added.

It further said that Afghan Taliban posts had also opened fire to support the infiltration attempt by the khawarij.

“The skilful and precise engagement by vigilant troops resulted in the killing of 12 khawarij and Afghan Taliban,” the statement said. During the exchange of fire, Naib Subedar Hidayat Aman was martyred after “fighting gallantly”.

This incident along the Pakistan-Afghanistan border vindicates Islamabad’s “objective and factual stance regarding the willful abject failure of the Afghan Taliban regime to deny the use of Afghan soil to the terrorist organisation”, the statement added.

“The security forces of Pakistan remain resolute and unwavering in their commitment to defend the nation’s frontiers,” said the ISPR, adding that sanitisation operation is being conducted in the area to eliminate any other Indian sponsored khawariji found in the area.”

“The relentless counter-terrorism campaign under vision Azm-i-Istehkam as approved by Federal Apex Committee on National Action Plan by security forces and law enforcement agencies of Pakistan will continue at full pace to wipe out the menace of foreign sponsored and supported terrorism from the country.”

“These sacrifices of our brave soldiers further reinforce our unwavering commitment to safeguarding our nation and its frontiers at all costs,” it said.

In a statement on X, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi paid tribute to the security forces for “foiling the infiltration attempt”.

He expressed “heartfelt condolences and expression of sympathy” to the bereaved family of the martyred Naib Subedar Hidayat Aman, adding that nation takes pride in the “professional capabilities and courage” of the security forces.

KP has been witnessing terrorist attacks and security challenges for a long time

September particularly witnessed a significant deterioration in Pakistan’s overall security environment, accompanied by growing political, economic and regional pressures, according to Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS).

Terrorist violence increased substantially, with 225 attacks recorded nationwide, compared with 199 in August, representing a 13.1 per cent increase and the highest monthly total recorded in 12 years.

On Sept 27, 14 people, including two rescue officials, were martyred and 35 sustained injuries after a suicide bomber rammed an explosive-laden vehicle into a police checkpost in and then targeted an ambulance taking bodies to hospital in DI Khan.

On Sept 18, a major attack in the old Police Lines in KP’s Kohat claimed 23 lives and injured about 100 others. Eight terrorists were killed during an overnight clearance operation.

    <!-- box/content -->
    <div dir='auto' class='story__content  flow-root    pt-1 mt-1 text-4 sm:text-4.5  overflow-visible'><p>Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi on Sunday chaired the first meeting of the KP Advisory Council, which was formed by the federal government following the <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2036352/emergency-governors-rule-imposed-in-kp-as-president-approves-cabinet-decision">imposition </a>of an emergency and governor’s rule in the province.</p>
<p>At the outset of the meeting, all members of the council introduced themselves and their portfolios.</p>
<p>Addressing the meeting, Kundi congratulated the members of the council, while noting that they would have to face many challenges. He said that they would get a briefing on the portfolios they had been assigned and would get a few days to familiarise themselves.</p>
<p>“We have to fast-track things. There will be zero tolerance on corruption. Things should be done in a timely manner,” he said, adding that they would have to demonstrate a clear difference from the work done by their predecessors.</p>
<p>He said that the first order of business was the law and order situation, adding that there should be no hesitation in taking inspiration from the other provinces.</p>
<p>He said that the current situation was an “opportunity” as he called for building the province’s soft image.</p>
<p>“If we have peace, we will get tourists and investors. My support is with you. I am available for you 24/7,” he said.</p>
    <figure class='media  w-full  w-full  media--  media--embed  media--uneven' data-original-src='https://www.youtube.com/shorts/VFBkI9uDbtk'>
        <div class='media__item  media__item--youtube_short  media__item--relative'>    <div style="position: relative; aspect-ratio: 9 / 16; overflow: hidden; max-width: 360px; margin: auto">
        <iframe
            src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/VFBkI9uDbtk?enablejsapi=1&controls=1&modestbranding=1&rel=0"
            style="position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; border: 0;"
            loading="lazy"
            allowfullscreen
        ></iframe>
    </div></div>
        
    </figure>
<p>Kundi then went on to read out a message for the people of the province, in which he said that due to “extraordinary circumstances”, “necessary measures” were taken under the Constitution.</p>
<p>He said that he would refrain from levelling allegations and political rhetoric.</p>
<p>“I have one message: peace, protection and stability have to be brought back to KP,” he said. He added that the people of KP had paid a huge price for the terrorism that plagued the province.</p>
<p>“The time has now come to give the people of the province, who have rendered these sacrifices, the right to peace. Our fight is against terrorism. Our fight is against the ideology and network which facilitates terrorism and weakens the implementation of the law,” he said.</p>
<p>He also said that Pakhtuns were not a cause of terrorism, but were the “biggest victims”. Therefore, the state had resolved that terrorism would be eliminated from KP and the people would be allowed to live their lives without fear.</p>
<p>“My first priority will be protecting the peace and the people. Right now, our biggest priority is taking effective steps against terrorism. For this, the capacity of the police and the Counter Terrorism Department will be increased,” he said.</p>
<p>He went on to say that another objective would be to cater to the people.</p>
<p>“Mere statements are not the real test of a government, rather the service it provides to the people,” he said. Kundi said that the council would focus on healthcare, education and employment.</p>
<p>The last objective, he said, would be to eliminate the whole ecosystem giving rise to terrorism in the province.</p>
<p>“We cannot solve the issue by just targeting terrorists. Those facilitating and financing … must be eliminated,” he said, adding that those involved in terrorism would be dealt with according to the law.</p>
<p>He assured the people of KP that the “extraordinary steps” taken were not meant to target a particular party or group. Kundi said that the main purpose was to ensure peace and security as he asked for their cooperation.</p>

headline: 'Our fight is against terrorism': Kundi chairs first meeting of KP Advisory Council
description: Tells council members first order of business is the law and order situation, and there should be no hesitation in taking inspiration from the other provinces.
author: News Desk
article_text:
Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi on Sunday chaired the first meeting of the KP Advisory Council, which was formed by the federal government following the imposition of an emergency and governor’s rule in the province.

At the outset of the meeting, all members of the council introduced themselves and their portfolios.

Addressing the meeting, Kundi congratulated the members of the council, while noting that they would have to face many challenges. He said that they would get a briefing on the portfolios they had been assigned and would get a few days to familiarise themselves.

“We have to fast-track things. There will be zero tolerance on corruption. Things should be done in a timely manner,” he said, adding that they would have to demonstrate a clear difference from the work done by their predecessors.

He said that the first order of business was the law and order situation, adding that there should be no hesitation in taking inspiration from the other provinces.

He said that the current situation was an “opportunity” as he called for building the province’s soft image.

“If we have peace, we will get tourists and investors. My support is with you. I am available for you 24/7,” he said.

Kundi then went on to read out a message for the people of the province, in which he said that due to “extraordinary circumstances”, “necessary measures” were taken under the Constitution.

He said that he would refrain from levelling allegations and political rhetoric.

“I have one message: peace, protection and stability have to be brought back to KP,” he said. He added that the people of KP had paid a huge price for the terrorism that plagued the province.

“The time has now come to give the people of the province, who have rendered these sacrifices, the right to peace. Our fight is against terrorism. Our fight is against the ideology and network which facilitates terrorism and weakens the implementation of the law,” he said.

He also said that Pakhtuns were not a cause of terrorism, but were the “biggest victims”. Therefore, the state had resolved that terrorism would be eliminated from KP and the people would be allowed to live their lives without fear.

“My first priority will be protecting the peace and the people. Right now, our biggest priority is taking effective steps against terrorism. For this, the capacity of the police and the Counter Terrorism Department will be increased,” he said.

He went on to say that another objective would be to cater to the people.

“Mere statements are not the real test of a government, rather the service it provides to the people,” he said. Kundi said that the council would focus on healthcare, education and employment.

The last objective, he said, would be to eliminate the whole ecosystem giving rise to terrorism in the province.

“We cannot solve the issue by just targeting terrorists. Those facilitating and financing … must be eliminated,” he said, adding that those involved in terrorism would be dealt with according to the law.

He assured the people of KP that the “extraordinary steps” taken were not meant to target a particular party or group. Kundi said that the main purpose was to ensure peace and security as he asked for their cooperation.

    <!-- box/content -->
    <div dir='auto' class='story__content  flow-root    pt-1 mt-1 text-4 sm:text-4.5  overflow-visible'><p>ISLAMABAD: The Tehreek-i-Tahafuz Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP) on Sunday condemned the imposition of <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2036352/emergency-governors-rule-imposed-in-kp-as-president-approves-cabinet-decision">governor’s rule and an emergency</a> in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, terming the move unconstitutional and contrary to democratic principles.</p>
<p>It announced that it would challenge governor’s rule through the courts, assemblies and public forums. It also said the long march would go ahead as planned.</p>
<p>Addressing a press conference, PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan said governor’s rule and an emergency would not resolve the province’s problems, stressing that counterterrorism efforts required a unified strategy developed through political consensus.</p>
<p>He rejected allegations that the KP government had <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2036389/info-minister-alleges-nexus-between-pti-led-kp-govt-terrorists">failed to cooperate</a> with the federal government in tackling terrorism, saying the provincial administration remained committed to eliminating the menace.</p>
<p>“If the problem of terrorism exists in 12 districts, why has governor’s rule been imposed across the province?” he asked.</p>
<p>Gohar said the PTI had consistently condemned terrorism in all its forms and maintained that the country’s security and defence remained paramount. However, he argued that counterterrorism measures should not be used to justify action against his party.</p>
<p>He said the PTI would challenge <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2036352/emergency-governors-rule-imposed-in-kp-as-president-approves-cabinet-decision">governor’s rule</a> through the courts, assemblies and public forums, adding that the party’s struggle for constitutional and democratic rights would continue.</p>
<p>The PTI chairman also called for the release of political prisoners and the restoration of the <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2034734">legal rights</a> of former prime minister and party founder Imran Khan. He demanded that Imran be transferred to a hospital for treatment, that his family be allowed to meet him, and that details of his health and treatment be shared with them.</p>
<p>Gohar said the party had approached the Supreme Court and high courts 19 times seeking relief for its incarcerated founder. He said the announcement of a long march for Aug 5 had been <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2024891">made to secure Imran’s rights</a> after the party failed to obtain relief through the courts.</p>
<p>He claimed that around 1,500 PTI workers were imprisoned in Punjab, while 10 members of the provincial assembly, including three ministers, and eight members of the National Assembly had also been arrested.</p>
<p>The PTI chairman rejected the <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2036389/info-minister-alleges-nexus-between-pti-led-kp-govt-terrorists">government’s narrative</a> about his party, arguing that political action against the PTI should not be linked to efforts to eliminate terrorism.</p>
<p>He further claimed that terrorism had not been discussed during 15 meetings with government representatives before Oct 2. He said the KP government had increased police capacity, provided security resources and participated in counterterrorism meetings.</p>
<p>Gohar said federal interference had weakened the provincial government’s authority, adding that sidelining an elected chief minister was inconsistent with democratic principles.</p>
<h2><a id="consensus-needed-on-counterterrorism" href="#consensus-needed-on-counterterrorism" class="heading-permalink" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1" title="Permalink"></a>Consensus needed on counterterrorism</h2>
<p>PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja said the party had consistently called for a mutually agreed strategy to address terrorism, arguing that decisions on security operations should be taken in consultation with all political parties.</p>
<p>Referring to the Parachinar agreement, he said the party’s position had remained clear and that it was seeking the implementation of previously agreed decisions rather than the introduction of new conditions.</p>
<p>He said the party had cited the February 2026 <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/1971238">meeting of the Apex Committee</a> and a resolution adopted at a peace jirga as the basis for moving forward.</p>
<p>Raja said Chief Minister Sohail Afridi had taken a clear position and that the provincial government could not grant the federal government unrestricted authority to undertake whatever measures it considered appropriate.</p>
<p>“We cannot give anyone written permission to do whatever they want and then endorse it,” he said.</p>
<p>He added that any decision concerning governor’s rule or an emergency must be made in accordance with constitutional principles and political consensus.</p>
<p>Raja said negotiations had involved consultations with Mahmood Khan Achakzai and Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, while Maulana Fazlur Rehman and other political leaders had been trying to ensure the process succeeded.</p>
<p>He claimed that the <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2034465">talks had been progressing satisfactorily</a> and that the imposition of an emergency was a hasty decision. He also cited Senator Kamran Murtaza as saying that negotiations were moving in the right direction.</p>
<p>The TTAP leader described the arrest of a provincial assembly speaker as an extraordinary step, adding that the assembly remained in existence.</p>
<p>Despite what he described as a crackdown on the PTI, Raja said the party remained committed to its principles and was seeking peace and protection for innocent people.</p>
<p>He confirmed that there had been no change to the announcement of the long march by Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, saying peaceful protest was a fundamental constitutional right.</p>
<p>“We will not throw stones. Through peaceful protest, we have to express our moral position,” he said, adding that a large-scale, peaceful demonstration by citizens across the country would convey a strong message.</p>
<p>He said people would decide how to express their displeasure over what he described as actions against democracy, while distinguishing between political protest and revolutionary action.</p>
<h2><a id="national-action-plan-must-be-implemented" href="#national-action-plan-must-be-implemented" class="heading-permalink" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1" title="Permalink"></a>National Action Plan must be implemented</h2>
<p>Majlis Wahdat-i-Muslimeen (MWM) chief Allama Raja Nasir Abbas said Pakistan was a federation whose provinces were united under a single Constitution, and criticised the treatment meted out to the PTI.</p>
<p>He claimed that Imran had received the majority of public support in the elections and alleged that the ruling establishment feared the public mandate and had continuously targeted the PTI.</p>
<p>Abbas blamed the government for the prevailing insecurity, saying the conduct of those in power had caused greater damage than the country’s external enemies could inflict.</p>
<p>He called for the implementation of the National Action Plan (NAP) and said the seven days since the start of negotiations could have been used to make progress towards a political settlement.</p>
<p>Abbas further said the party could not support military operations in which ordinary citizens became victims, stressing that counterterrorism measures must protect civilians and contribute to lasting peace.</p>

headline: TTAP condemns imposition of governor’s rule, emergency in KP, calls move 'unconstitutional'
description: Opposition alliance announces plans to challenge governor’s rule through courts, assemblies and public forums.
author: Ikram Junaidi
article_text:
ISLAMABAD: The Tehreek-i-Tahafuz Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP) on Sunday condemned the imposition of governor’s rule and an emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, terming the move unconstitutional and contrary to democratic principles.

It announced that it would challenge governor’s rule through the courts, assemblies and public forums. It also said the long march would go ahead as planned.

Addressing a press conference, PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan said governor’s rule and an emergency would not resolve the province’s problems, stressing that counterterrorism efforts required a unified strategy developed through political consensus.

He rejected allegations that the KP government had failed to cooperate with the federal government in tackling terrorism, saying the provincial administration remained committed to eliminating the menace.

“If the problem of terrorism exists in 12 districts, why has governor’s rule been imposed across the province?” he asked.

Gohar said the PTI had consistently condemned terrorism in all its forms and maintained that the country’s security and defence remained paramount. However, he argued that counterterrorism measures should not be used to justify action against his party.

He said the PTI would challenge governor’s rule through the courts, assemblies and public forums, adding that the party’s struggle for constitutional and democratic rights would continue.

The PTI chairman also called for the release of political prisoners and the restoration of the legal rights of former prime minister and party founder Imran Khan. He demanded that Imran be transferred to a hospital for treatment, that his family be allowed to meet him, and that details of his health and treatment be shared with them.

Gohar said the party had approached the Supreme Court and high courts 19 times seeking relief for its incarcerated founder. He said the announcement of a long march for Aug 5 had been made to secure Imran’s rights after the party failed to obtain relief through the courts.

He claimed that around 1,500 PTI workers were imprisoned in Punjab, while 10 members of the provincial assembly, including three ministers, and eight members of the National Assembly had also been arrested.

The PTI chairman rejected the government’s narrative about his party, arguing that political action against the PTI should not be linked to efforts to eliminate terrorism.

He further claimed that terrorism had not been discussed during 15 meetings with government representatives before Oct 2. He said the KP government had increased police capacity, provided security resources and participated in counterterrorism meetings.

Gohar said federal interference had weakened the provincial government’s authority, adding that sidelining an elected chief minister was inconsistent with democratic principles.

Consensus needed on counterterrorism

PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja said the party had consistently called for a mutually agreed strategy to address terrorism, arguing that decisions on security operations should be taken in consultation with all political parties.

Referring to the Parachinar agreement, he said the party’s position had remained clear and that it was seeking the implementation of previously agreed decisions rather than the introduction of new conditions.

He said the party had cited the February 2026 meeting of the Apex Committee and a resolution adopted at a peace jirga as the basis for moving forward.

Raja said Chief Minister Sohail Afridi had taken a clear position and that the provincial government could not grant the federal government unrestricted authority to undertake whatever measures it considered appropriate.

“We cannot give anyone written permission to do whatever they want and then endorse it,” he said.

He added that any decision concerning governor’s rule or an emergency must be made in accordance with constitutional principles and political consensus.

Raja said negotiations had involved consultations with Mahmood Khan Achakzai and Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, while Maulana Fazlur Rehman and other political leaders had been trying to ensure the process succeeded.

He claimed that the talks had been progressing satisfactorily and that the imposition of an emergency was a hasty decision. He also cited Senator Kamran Murtaza as saying that negotiations were moving in the right direction.

The TTAP leader described the arrest of a provincial assembly speaker as an extraordinary step, adding that the assembly remained in existence.

Despite what he described as a crackdown on the PTI, Raja said the party remained committed to its principles and was seeking peace and protection for innocent people.

He confirmed that there had been no change to the announcement of the long march by Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, saying peaceful protest was a fundamental constitutional right.

“We will not throw stones. Through peaceful protest, we have to express our moral position,” he said, adding that a large-scale, peaceful demonstration by citizens across the country would convey a strong message.

He said people would decide how to express their displeasure over what he described as actions against democracy, while distinguishing between political protest and revolutionary action.

National Action Plan must be implemented

Majlis Wahdat-i-Muslimeen (MWM) chief Allama Raja Nasir Abbas said Pakistan was a federation whose provinces were united under a single Constitution, and criticised the treatment meted out to the PTI.

He claimed that Imran had received the majority of public support in the elections and alleged that the ruling establishment feared the public mandate and had continuously targeted the PTI.

Abbas blamed the government for the prevailing insecurity, saying the conduct of those in power had caused greater damage than the country’s external enemies could inflict.

He called for the implementation of the National Action Plan (NAP) and said the seven days since the start of negotiations could have been used to make progress towards a political settlement.

Abbas further said the party could not support military operations in which ordinary citizens became victims, stressing that counterterrorism measures must protect civilians and contribute to lasting peace.

ISLAMABAD: The Tehreek-i-Tahafuz Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP) on Sunday condemned the imposition of governor’s rule and an emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, terming the move unconstitutional and contrary to democratic principles.

It announced that it would challenge governor’s rule through the courts, assemblies and public forums. It also said the long march would go ahead as planned.

Addressing a press conference, PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan said governor’s rule and an emergency would not resolve the province’s problems, stressing that counterterrorism efforts required a unified strategy developed through political consensus.

He rejected allegations that the KP government had failed to cooperate with the federal government in tackling terrorism, saying the provincial administration remained committed to eliminating the menace.

“If the problem of terrorism exists in 12 districts, why has governor’s rule been imposed across the province?” he asked.

Gohar said the PTI had consistently condemned terrorism in all its forms and maintained that the country’s security and defence remained paramount. However, he argued that counterterrorism measures should not be used to justify action against his party.

He said the PTI would challenge governor’s rule through the courts, assemblies and public forums, adding that the party’s struggle for constitutional and democratic rights would continue.

The PTI chairman also called for the release of political prisoners and the restoration of the legal rights of former prime minister and party founder Imran Khan. He demanded that Imran be transferred to a hospital for treatment, that his family be allowed to meet him, and that details of his health and treatment be shared with them.

Gohar said the party had approached the Supreme Court and high courts 19 times seeking relief for its incarcerated founder. He said the announcement of a long march for Aug 5 had been made to secure Imran’s rights after the party failed to obtain relief through the courts.

He claimed that around 1,500 PTI workers were imprisoned in Punjab, while 10 members of the provincial assembly, including three ministers, and eight members of the National Assembly had also been arrested.

The PTI chairman rejected the government’s narrative about his party, arguing that political action against the PTI should not be linked to efforts to eliminate terrorism.

He further claimed that terrorism had not been discussed during 15 meetings with government representatives before Oct 2. He said the KP government had increased police capacity, provided security resources and participated in counterterrorism meetings.

Gohar said federal interference had weakened the provincial government’s authority, adding that sidelining an elected chief minister was inconsistent with democratic principles.

Consensus needed on counterterrorism

PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja said the party had consistently called for a mutually agreed strategy to address terrorism, arguing that decisions on security operations should be taken in consultation with all political parties.

Referring to the Parachinar agreement, he said the party’s position had remained clear and that it was seeking the implementation of previously agreed decisions rather than the introduction of new conditions.

He said the party had cited the February 2026 meeting of the Apex Committee and a resolution adopted at a peace jirga as the basis for moving forward.

Raja said Chief Minister Sohail Afridi had taken a clear position and that the provincial government could not grant the federal government unrestricted authority to undertake whatever measures it considered appropriate.

“We cannot give anyone written permission to do whatever they want and then endorse it,” he said.

He added that any decision concerning governor’s rule or an emergency must be made in accordance with constitutional principles and political consensus.

Raja said negotiations had involved consultations with Mahmood Khan Achakzai and Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, while Maulana Fazlur Rehman and other political leaders had been trying to ensure the process succeeded.

He claimed that the talks had been progressing satisfactorily and that the imposition of an emergency was a hasty decision. He also cited Senator Kamran Murtaza as saying that negotiations were moving in the right direction.

The TTAP leader described the arrest of a provincial assembly speaker as an extraordinary step, adding that the assembly remained in existence.

Despite what he described as a crackdown on the PTI, Raja said the party remained committed to its principles and was seeking peace and protection for innocent people.

He confirmed that there had been no change to the announcement of the long march by Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, saying peaceful protest was a fundamental constitutional right.

“We will not throw stones. Through peaceful protest, we have to express our moral position,” he said, adding that a large-scale, peaceful demonstration by citizens across the country would convey a strong message.

He said people would decide how to express their displeasure over what he described as actions against democracy, while distinguishing between political protest and revolutionary action.

National Action Plan must be implemented

Majlis Wahdat-i-Muslimeen (MWM) chief Allama Raja Nasir Abbas said Pakistan was a federation whose provinces were united under a single Constitution, and criticised the treatment meted out to the PTI.

He claimed that Imran had received the majority of public support in the elections and alleged that the ruling establishment feared the public mandate and had continuously targeted the PTI.

Abbas blamed the government for the prevailing insecurity, saying the conduct of those in power had caused greater damage than the country’s external enemies could inflict.

He called for the implementation of the National Action Plan (NAP) and said the seven days since the start of negotiations could have been used to make progress towards a political settlement.

Abbas further said the party could not support military operations in which ordinary citizens became victims, stressing that counterterrorism measures must protect civilians and contribute to lasting peace.

    <script>

    });

    googletag.cmd.push(function() {

            .defineSizeMapping([[[0,0],[[300,250]]]])

            .defineSizeMapping([[[970,0],[[728,90],[320,50],[320,100],[300,50],[970,250],[970,90]]],[[728,0],[[728,90],[320,50],[320,100],[300,50]]],[[0,0],[[300,250],[320,50],[320,100],[300,50]]]])

            .addService(googletag.pubads());

            .defineSizeMapping([])
            .addService(googletag.pubads());
        
                    
        googletag.setConfig({
            lazyLoad: {
                fetchMarginPercent: -1,
                renderMarginPercent: -1,
                mobileScaling: 1.0,
